cohort: The study included 33,003 low-risk women with singleton pregnancies at or beyond 41 completed weeks of gestation from 292 facilities across 21 countries.
finding: Compared to induction of labour, elective caesarean section significantly increased the risk of NICU admission, while expectant management was associated with a decreased risk of caesarean section.
mod_finding: Compared to Induction of Labour (IOL), Elective Caesarean Section (ECS) significantly increased the risk of NICU admission, and Expectant Management (EM) was significantly associated with decreased risk of Caesarean section.
country: Africa, Asia, Latin America, Middle East (21 countries)
birth_weight: Adjusted for birth weight, but no specific weight range for inclusion was mentioned.
